title: Generative AI for Computer Vision - Week 9 Assignment 9
subject: Generative AI for Computer Vision

questions.question: 1. What is the main purpose of a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)?
options: To generate new data similar to the training data
questions.correctAnswer: To generate new data similar to the training data
questions.explanation: The main purpose of a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) is to generate new, synthetic data samples that closely mimic the distribution of the training data.

questions.question: 2. A GAN mainly consists of which two networks?
questions.explanation: A GAN consists of two competing neural networks: a Generator that creates synthetic data samples and a Discriminator that distinguishes between real and generated samples.

questions.question: 3. What is the main role of the Generator in a GAN?
options: To distinguish real and fake data
To remove noise from the dataset
questions.explanation: The Generator takes random noise as input and maps it to realistic synthetic data samples aimed at deceiving the Discriminator.

questions.question: 4. What is a common problem when training GANs?
questions.explanation: Mode collapse is a classic failure mode during GAN training where the Generator produces only a limited variety of outputs, repeatedly generating the same or similar samples.

questions.question: 5. What is the main idea of a Conditional GAN (cGAN)?
options: It generates data based on additional information such as class labels
It does not use a Discriminator
It can only generate random noise
questions.correctAnswer: It generates data based on additional information such as class labels
questions.explanation: Conditional GANs (cGANs) condition both the Generator and Discriminator on additional auxiliary information (such as class labels or text) to control the generation process.

questions.question: 6. What is the main purpose of Wasserstein GAN (WGAN)?
options: To improve the stability of GAN training
questions.correctAnswer: To improve the stability of GAN training
questions.explanation: Wasserstein GAN utilizes the Earth Mover's (Wasserstein-1) Distance to provide smooth, meaningful gradients everywhere, significantly improving training stability and alleviating mode collapse.

questions.question: 7. What happens during the forward diffusion process in a diffusion model?
options: The model directly generates the final image
Noise is completely removed from the data
Noise is gradually added to the data
questions.correctAnswer: Noise is gradually added to the data
questions.explanation: In the forward diffusion process, Gaussian noise is gradually added to an image across discrete time steps until it becomes pure random noise.

questions.question: 8. What happens during reverse diffusion?
options: Noise is gradually removed to generate data
questions.correctAnswer: Noise is gradually removed to generate data
questions.explanation: In reverse diffusion, a trained neural network iteratively predicts and removes noise from a random Gaussian sample to synthesize a clean, high-quality image.

questions.question: 9. What is the full form of DDPM?
questions.explanation: DDPM stands for Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model, a foundational class of generative models introduced by Ho et al. (2020).

questions.question: 10. What is the main purpose of the ELBO in a VAE or diffusion-model formulation?
options: To provide an objective for learning the generative model
questions.correctAnswer: To provide an objective for learning the generative model
questions.explanation: The Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO) provides a mathematically tractable surrogate objective function to maximize the log-likelihood of observed data in latent variable models.
